correctness.rationale: A geometric invariant-face argument identifies the fixed set with the monomer-dimer tile-packing complex for arbitrary finite simple H. Every tile set extends to a prism perfect matching by adding remaining rungs. The pivot-free-vertex monomer toggle is globally acyclic since dimer sets never increase on the reversed Hasse graph and its pivot monomer can never be removed along a directed cycle. Critical cells are one vertex and p(H) faces of dimension n/2-1, hence the claimed integral homotopy types including zero-dimensional boundary; all details reconstructed and independent finite checks replayed.

Published work on matching complexes and perfect-matching complexes generally studies different face conditions: disjoint edge sets or sets extendible to a perfect matching, not geometric layer-fixed spaces.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns geometric layer-fixed spaces of perfect-matching complexes of arbitrary Cartesian prisms, which are not recovered from the published nonequivariant homotopy types of Möbius/circular ladders or honeycombs. Explicit search of monomer-dimer equivalents, fixed-point formulations and stronger graph-prism results found no implication. The expanded arXiv manuscript remains an acknowledged full-text access risk.
residual_risks: The arXiv:2608.30601v2 expanded full text was inaccessible and could in principle include the orbit-barycenter fixed-point lemma or a stronger theorem.
An equivalent result may have appeared under the names monomer-dimer packing complex, independence complex of a tile-conflict graph, or as unpublished equivariant matching-complex work.
Search coverage and partitioning cannot establish uniqueness.

value.rationale: For a canonical graph involution, the full integral fixed-space homotopy type of arbitrary Cartesian prism perfect-matching complexes is determined by the natural perfect-matching enumeration p(H), a #P-hard graph count, giving substantive representation-theoretic/topological information not implied by nonequivariant graph-complex classifications. It covers highly nontrivial H (e.g. complete bipartite and disconnected) and specializes to an explicit circular-ladder Lefschetz number; not an arbitrary parameter exercise.
